To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transgenic alfalfa lines with introduced gene for the AMV coat protein had a significant effect on the density of some groups of bacteria in the rhizo sphere, and that the metabolic activity of the microbial community was not affected by the presence of the introduced gene in transgenic plants.
the transgenic alfalfa rhizospheres were characterized by the lower density of aerobic bacteria and the lower utilization rate of C-sources in comparison to non-transgenic alfalfas.
transgenic alfalfa lines, compared with their non-transgenics, had a significant effect on the density and diversity of aerobic bacteria in their rhizospheres.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of transgenesis on the diversity of rhizospheres microflora.
the effect of transgene on rhizosphere microbiota.
a new approach in the evaluation of transgenic alfafa plants on the microbial community in the rhizospheres, based on the cultivation-dependent platings and the Biolog™ method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transgenic alfalfa lines had no negative effect on the rhizosphere microbial population.
the introduced gene for AMVcp-s did not affect the microbial diversity in the rhizospheres.
the rhizosphere microbiota of transgenic alfafa plants is not affected in a negative way, but rather that transgenic alfalfa may even have positive effects on the soil microorganisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transgenic alfalfa clones did not significantly change the microbial community structure and the metabolic diversity of the rhizospheric microbial community.
transgenic alfalfa clones expressing the AMV cp-s gene did not have any significant impact on the microbial community structure of the alfalfa rhizosphere.
the transgenic alfalfa lines did not have a significant influence on the microbial communities of rhizospheres in comparison with non-transgenic alfalfas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transgenic alfalfa line GTL4/403-1, which is a clone with the highest expression of the AMVcp gene, had a significant effect on the density and metabolic profile of rhizospheres microorganisms.
transgenic alfalfa lines with introduced gene for AMVcp-s had no negative effect on the rhizosphere microbial diversity and physiological profiles.
the rhizosphere of transgenic and nontransgenic alfalfa clones is inhabited by different groups of soil microorganisms, and their densities are different.
